episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — November 5, 2026

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — November 8, 2026

The on-chain dollar just posted its steepest weekly contraction of the year, and the spot Bitcoin ETFs leaked right alongside it. Those are crypto's two institutional cash doors, and both were open at the same time.

Two days out, there's genuine news, but it comes from the wrong capital. Beijing still has not published a formal notice extending that suspension.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — November 8, 2026
episodes.summary: On Tuesday this desk told you that memory makers' share prices and their contract prices were telling two different stories, and that one of those signals would prove wrong. Since then, the gap has only widened. The stocks kept falling. The fundamental signals we can verify still point to a tighter market.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — November 8, 2026

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — November 8, 2026
episodes.summary: This week's open question in enterprise software has been whether usage-based pricing is running into budget caps, or whether the market simply grades the forward guide. Datadog's print is the last test of that idea this week. Palantir adds a filed backlog number.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — November 8, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's thesis has two parts. The newest human data again shows AI earning its keep as a selector of what to hit, not as a designer of the molecule itself. And the field's most-cited AI-designed drug turns out to have a thinner verified record than this show has been telling you.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — November 8, 2026
episodes.summary: Humanoids are still stuck proving who actually pays for them. Meanwhile, the biggest money in physical AI keeps landing on narrow autonomy that already works in the field. This week's largest check came from Shield AI, which agreed to pay up for a sensor it doesn't make.

Two companies are now running opposite bets on who owns the terrestrial network, and a catalyst-heavy week follows.
